$$\begin{aligned} y &= -x^3 + 3x^2 - 1 \\ \dfrac{dy}{dx} &= -3x^2 + 6x \\ &= 3x(2 - x) \end{aligned}$$
When $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$, we have $3x(2-x) = 0$.
$$x = 0, \qquad x = 2$$
$$y = -1 \qquad y = -2^3 + 3(2)^2 - 1 = 3$$
Stationary points are $(0, -1)$ and $(2, 3)$.
$$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -6x + 6$$
When $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0$, we have $6(1-x) = 0$.
$$x = 1$$
$$\begin{aligned} y &= -1^3 + 3\times 1^2 - 1 \\ &= 1 \end{aligned}$$
The point of inflection is $(1, 1)$.

\exfigure{33_q16_1}

solutions.latex:
$$\dfrac{dP}{dx} = 2 - \dfrac{72}{x^2}$$
Setting $\dfrac{dP}{dx} = 0$, we have
$$\begin{aligned} 2 &= \dfrac{72}{x^2} \\ x^2 &= 36 \\ x &= 6 \quad (\text{since } x > 0) \end{aligned}$$
$$\dfrac{d^2P}{dx^2} = \dfrac{144}{x^3}$$
When $x = 6$,
$$\dfrac{d^2P}{dx^2} = \dfrac{144}{6^3} \text{ which is greater than zero.}$$
$\therefore$ $P$ is a minimum when $x = 6$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{The minimum perimeter} &= 2\times 6 + \dfrac{72}{6} \\ &= 12 + 12 \\ &= 24 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} y &= c\ln x \\ \dfrac{dy}{dx} &= \dfrac{c}{x} \end{aligned}$$
The gradient of the tangent at $x = p$ is $\dfrac{c}{p}$.

At $x = p$, $y = c\ln p$
$$\begin{aligned} \therefore\ y - c\ln p &= \dfrac{c}{p}(x - p) \\ \therefore\ y - c\ln p &= \dfrac{c}{p}x - c \\ \therefore\ y &= \dfrac{c}{p}x - c + c\ln p \end{aligned}$$
